Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> CLOGSAG demands probe into alleged assault on Okaikwei North Assembly worker Source : Myjoyonline.com 27 November 2026 4:38am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Civil and Local Government Staff Association of Ghana (CLOGSAG) has called for a full-scale investigation into the alleged slapping of an administrative officer of the Okaikwei North Municipal Assembly, warning that violence against public servants cannot be tolerated in the workplace.
The demand follows the circulation of a video purportedly showing the Personal Assistant to the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE), Christian Tetteh Badger, striking an assembly staff member, Jeffrey De-Graft Johnson, during a confrontation reportedly over a speech prepared for the MCE.
The aide has since been suspended, while the case has been referred to the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service for further investigation.
In a statement issued on Thursday, November 26, CLOGSAG said it was deeply troubled by the incident, describing the alleged conduct as a violation of the dignity and professional rights of public service employees.
CLOGSAG said disagreements over official assignments or administrative matters could not justify physical attacks, intimidation or humiliation of workers.
“CLOGSAG unequivocally condemns any form of violence, intimidation, harassment or victimisation against public servants in the discharge of their official duties,” the statement said.
It wants the Office of the Head of the Local Government Service and other relevant oversight institutions to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident and determine whether any administrative or disciplinary rules have been breached.
CLOGSAG has also urged the police to pursue their investigations and take appropriate legal action against anyone found to have committed an offence.
CLOGSAG said it stood with Mr Johnson and other employees of the Local Government Service, adding that it would use all lawful means available to defend the rights, welfare and safety of its members.
“The Association will pursue all legitimate and lawful avenues available to ensure that the rights and interests of its members are adequately protected,” it said.
The incident has drawn attention to workplace conduct and the treatment of public servants, particularly the responsibility of officials in public institutions to resolve professional disagreements without resorting to intimidation or violence.
